highlights: OpenAI chief scientist Jakub Pachocki proposes perplexity as a metric to compare model developers and inform shared safety standards, and publishes OpenAI's internal pretraining measurements.
Dragos sent nearly two million canary-laced prompts to AI services and found data from at least three providers exposed, with Zero Data Retention flags often ignored.
On the open-weight side, inclusionAI released the 560B medical model LingSante-3.1-flash and OVHcloud released Olala-v1.0-mini-7A1B, which runs on a laptop.

items.title: OpenAI's chief scientist proposes perplexity as a shared progress metric
items.summary: In a new post, Jakub Pachocki argues for establishing perplexity (cross-entropy loss) as a metric to compare model developers and inform shared safety standards, and publishes OpenAI's internal pretraining perplexity measurements; he says a model at log-perplexity ~0.76 started producing groundbreaking results on open math problems. He also proposes common limits, based on perplexity and other measurements, that developers would not cross until AI monitoring reaches a concrete milestone. Since chain-of-thought gains do not show up in perplexity, developers should read it as a gauge of pretraining progress rather than a replacement for task evals.

evidence.quote: By Jakub Pachocki, Chief Scientist at OpenAI

I argue for establishing perplexity (or, equivalently, cross-entropy loss) as a metric to compare between model developers and inform shared safety standards. As a first step, I provide more transparency into pretraining progress at OpenAI.
Once we upgraded to a model of log-perplexity ~0.76, it started producing groundbreaking results.

I further propose common limits , based on perplexity and other measurements, that developers are committed to not crossing until our ability to understand and monitor AI behavior achieves a certain concrete milestone
chain-of-thought reasoning does not reduce perplexity achieved by the model, even though it leads to a drastic increase in capabilities.

items.title: Dragos canary tokens expose breached AI providers and leaked prompts
items.summary: Over five months Dragos sent approximately two million prompts carrying unique URLs and canary credentials to widely used AI services, and found data from at least three providers exposed, none of which knew until notified; resellers on an inference marketplace could view and retain customer prompts with standard logging. A Chinese AI lab fetched secret URLs from more than half of the prompts sent to its models, including roughly two-thirds of requests marked Zero Data Retention. Developers routing through resellers should treat secrets and internal links in prompts as potentially leaked, and not rely on ZDR flags.

evidence.quote: we submitted approximately two million prompts containing unique URLs and canary token credentials to widely used AI services and monitored what happened after inference.
We observed activity indicating that data from at least three AI providers was exposed.
The earliest incident dates back to the middle of July, and none of the three providers knew about their breach until we notified them.

Multiple resellers operating through an AI inference marketplace were able to view and retain customer prompts using standard logging capabilities, without exploiting a vulnerability or bypassing platform controls.

fetched the secret URLs from more than half of the prompts that we sent to its models between July and October, including roughly two-thirds of the requests marked as “no data collection” or Zero Data Retention.

items.title: inclusionAI releases LingSante-3.1-flash, a 560B medical MoE with 25B active
items.summary: inclusionAI's open-weight medical MoE LingSante-3.1-flash is built on Ling-3.1-flash, with 560B total parameters, 25B active per token and a 1M-token context, targeting medical reasoning, healthcare communication, evidence-based research and long-horizon medical tasks; the model card says it ranks second overall behind only GPT-6 Astra on medical professional behavior benchmarks. It ships under MIT with vLLM and SGLang instructions, and the card stresses it is for research and evaluation, not a medical device or an independent basis for diagnosis or treatment.

evidence.quote: Built on Ling-3.1-flash , it has 560 billion total parameters , activates 25 billion parameters per token , and supports a 1-million-token context window .
Architecture Hybrid-linear MoE Total parameters 560B Activated parameters per token 25B Context window 1M tokens
LingSante-3.1-flash demonstrates strong performance on benchmarks for medical professional behavior, ranking second overall behind only GPT-6 Astra.
LingSante-3.1-flash is intended for research and evaluation. It is not a medical device and must not be used as an independent basis for diagnosis, prescriptions, or treatment.

items.title: OVHcloud releases Olala-v1.0-mini-7A1B: 6.8B total, about 1B active
items.summary: OVHai LLM, part of the OVHcloud group, released Olala-v1.0-mini-7A1B, a small reasoning model for chat, instruction following and tool use built on a hybrid Mamba-3 / attention mixture-of-experts architecture, with 6.8B total and about 1B active parameters; only 7 of its 36 layers keep a KV cache, and context is 32K. It was trained on 12.8T tokens on three European supercomputers and released with open weights under Apache 2.0. Developers get a commercially usable small model that runs on a laptop, or can call it through OVHcloud AI Endpoints' OpenAI-compatible API.

evidence.quote: is a small reasoning model for chat, instruction following and tool use , built on our hybrid Mamba-3 / attention mixture-of-experts architecture.

designed in France by OVHai LLM (OVHcloud group), trained on three European supercomputers (JUPITER, Jean Zay and MeluXina) on 12.8T tokens of public datasets and our own synthetic data, and released with open weights under Apache 2.0.
Efficient: about 1B active parameters per token, and only 7 of its 36 layers keep a KV cache. It runs on a laptop.
Parameters 6.8B total, about 1B active per token
Context length 32K tokens (input + output)
OVHcloud AI Endpoints A production API, OpenAI-compatible, hosted in Europe

items.title: KAIST's KORMo-Web-11B is a Korean-English web agent driven by screenshots
items.summary: KAIST MLP Lab's KORMo-Web-11B extends the from-scratch KORMo-10B language model through KORMo-VL into a web agent while preserving its LLM and VLM capabilities, operating primarily through screenshots without a full DOM. On Online-Mind2Web it scores 31.3 in English and 33.7 in Korean, beating the strongest non-KORMo open-weight baseline on Korean by 13.5 percentage points while trailing OpenWebRL-4B (32.7) in English. Weights are Apache-2.0 with a vLLM inference path and browser harness, a fit for Korean-language browser automation.

evidence.quote: Developed from the KORMo-10B language model, trained from scratch by KAIST MLP Lab, and extended through KORMo-VL into a web agent.
KORMo-Web-11B is designed to preserve its original LLM and VLM capabilities while learning to act as a GUI agent.
Visual-First Web Interaction: Operates primarily through screenshots without requiring full DOM or accessibility trees.
OpenWebRL-4B 4B 32.7 15.4 KORMo-Web-11B (ours) 11B 31.3 33.7
KORMo-Web-11B achieves 33.7% Korean task success , exceeding the strongest non-KORMo open-weight baseline listed above by 13.5 percentage points .
Includes model weights, Transformers 5 support, a vLLM inference path, browser harness, and reference inference settings.
Built on KORMo-VL and KORMo-10B by KAIST MLP Lab. Evaluated on Online-Mind2Web and its Korean counterpart.

items.title: tiny-voca: a 4.5M-parameter English TTS that runs about 70x real time on CPU
items.summary: n4ze3m's tiny-voca is an English text-to-speech model with two voices, F2 and M2, that has 4.5M parameters including the waveform generator, was trained from scratch on about 18 hours of synthetic speech, and outputs 24 kHz mono audio. The card says it runs about 70x faster than real time on four CPU threads, and it ships PyTorch weights and an ONNX export under Apache-2.0. It is worth a try for on-device or GPU-free English TTS.

evidence.quote: tiny-voca is a small English text-to-speech model with two voices, F2 (female) and M2 (male). The complete model, including the waveform generator, has 4.5M parameters and was trained from scratch on about 18 hours of synthetic speech. It runs about 70x faster than real time on four CPU threads.
Voices F2, M2 (American English) Output 24 kHz mono
onnx/model.onnx 21.4 MB ONNX export, float32, opset 17

items.title: Grid Robotics proposes an evaluation framework and roadmap for agentic robotics
items.summary: This position paper from Grid Robotics and coauthors argues that the release of GPT-6 Astra marks a new paradigm of agentic robotics, with an Embodied System 2 made of a foundation model plus an embodied harness as the decision-making core, whose challenge is turning general reasoning into verifiable actions under physical constraints. It proposes an evaluation framework measuring both model capabilities and closed-loop system performance, plus a research roadmap toward sustained autonomy. Builders of embodied agents get shared definitions and evaluation dimensions to align on.

evidence.quote: We argue that Embodied System 2 , realized by a foundation model together with an embodied harness , forms the decision-making core of agentic robotics .
we propose an evaluation framework that measures both model capabilities and closed-loop system performance.

we envision a research roadmap toward sustained autonomy : the ability to perform work safely and reliably with progressively broader responsibility, from executing individual primitives to fulfilling standing roles.

items.title: mod_wsgi's creator builds Muru, an AI-assisted Rust server for Python apps
items.summary: Graham Dumpleton, who started mod_wsgi, released Muru, an AI-assisted Rust server for running ASGI and WSGI Python apps in both development and production, and has been documenting its development in detail. He says the AI may do a lot of the surface work, but deciding what isn't good enough yet is still down to him. Python web developers get a new serving option to watch, and a detailed record of an experienced developer building infrastructure with AI.

evidence.quote: Muru is his new, AI-assisted Rust server that aims to provide the best possible tools for running ASGI and WSGI Python apps both in development and production.
The AI may be doing a lot of the work on the surface, but deciding what isn't good enough yet is still down to me
